paper.purpose: The page. The stock everything is printed on.

surface.purpose: Cards, inputs, raised rows — the lightest plane.

surface-sunken.purpose: The one surface that goes down — segmented track, icon wells.

hairline.purpose: Every resting edge in the app.

ink.purpose: Primary text, and the dark primary-button fill.

body-ink.purpose: Long-form message copy, a touch softer than ink.

faint-ink.purpose: Metadata and timestamps. The AA-corrected floor, not the design's original value.

brand-blue.purpose: Every primary action, selection and link.

brand-blue-deep.purpose: Brand headings and strong brand text.

brand-tile.purpose: Fixed in BOTH appearances — the solid tile behind the logo and lock marks.

gold.purpose: Unread, and the compose FAB. Nothing else.

gold-ink.purpose: Gold at a strength that can be SEEN — the unread ring, the attention numeral, the FAB's edge.

gold-soft.purpose: The test-env banner, the cost card, the re-auth strip.

violet.purpose: The compose draft marker, and one of the six avatar hues.

success.purpose: A completed delivery, a free message.

danger.purpose: Destructive actions and terminal delivery failures.

display.purpose: The main screen title — home and welcome only.  Bricolage ExtraBold.

headline.purpose: Stack-header titles, dialog titles, a message subject.  Bricolage ExtraBold.

title.purpose: Section headers, a box owner's name.  Bricolage Bold.

body.purpose: Primary readable text.  Public Sans Regular.

label.purpose: Form and metadata field labels.  Public Sans SemiBold.

shadows.name: depth.lg
shadows.purpose: Dialogs. A layered stack — inset top highlight, tight contact shadow, soft ambient — so it reads in both appearances.

shadows.name: depth.md
shadows.purpose: Defined and deliberately unused. Tonal layering covers this level.

shadows.name: fab-lift
shadows.purpose: The compose FAB. Gold-tinted atmosphere; the FAB's actual boundary is a 1px gold-ink outline.

shadows.name: emblem-lift
shadows.purpose: The 96dp brand tile on a success screen.

shadows.name: knob
shadows.purpose: The switch knob. One soft drop — no inset, no ambient layer.

motion.name: press-dip
motion.purpose: A press is answered by a dip, not a bop. No spring, no overshoot.

motion.name: refusal
motion.purpose: A blocked button answers instead of swallowing the press. Occupies no layout space.

motion.name: sync-sweep
motion.value: translateX -110% → 320% of bar width / 1300ms / ease-in-out / infinite
motion.purpose: The 3px reserved sync strip. Shown static under Reduce Motion.

motion.name: reduce-motion
motion.value: every animation above yields; haptics and focus changes survive
motion.purpose: A refusal still refuses without moving.

breakpoints.name: content-max
breakpoints.value: 720dp — ContentColumn caps and centres; margins take the rest

breakpoints.name: large-screen
breakpoints.value: >= 600dp — governed by the OS from Android 16; orientation locks are ignored

narrative.overview:
Obálka means envelope. The system takes that literally, and the literalism is what makes it decidable: paper #F4EEE2 is the stock, surface #FFFDF8 is the enclosed sheet, hairline #ECE3D2 is the fold, ink #211B12 is what was printed on it. When a question comes up about a new surface, the envelope answers it before taste has to.

The app holds legally binding government mail: records with consequences, deadlines that expire, and a delivery fiction that lands whether or not anyone opened the message. The design's whole job is to carry that weight without feeling like a government form. Warmth does the humanity, precision does the authority, and neither is allowed to borrow from the other.

The system replaced a cool-navy neutral ramp in feature 009. That is the one confirmed anti-reference: not cool greys, not a blue-tinted "productivity app" neutral. The brand blue and gold survived the change; the greys did not.
keyCharacteristics: Warm neutrals throughout — there is no true grey and no pure white anywhere in the palette.
Two families, strictly divided: Bricolage Grotesque says what a thing is, Public Sans says what it contains.
Depth is tone, not shadow. Dark mode raises by getting lighter.
One accent doing one job: gold means unread, and almost nothing else.
Nothing moves once it is on screen. Space is reserved before it is needed.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Gold means unread. It is also spent on the compose FAB, because composing is the one action the inbox exists to offer — and nowhere else. A second gold thing on a screen makes the first one stop meaning anything.

rules.name: The On-X Rule
rules.body: A token named on-<something> is safe only on that something. on-blue is ink that sits on brand-blue; in dark mode it is near-black, because dark mode's blue is bright. Anything painted on a fill that does not follow the theme — an avatar hue, the brand tile, a switch knob — takes on-solid, which is white in both appearances. This rule exists because it was broken: on-blue was silently doing both jobs, and when dark mode's blue was brightened, every avatar monogram in the app fell to 2.1–3.0:1.

rules.name: The Measured Palette Rule
rules.body: Every foreground/background pair the app renders is asserted in __tests__/theme/contrast.test.ts, and the pairs are derived from where tokens are painted, not transcribed. A palette is edited by eye, and a number that used to pass is exactly the thing nobody re-measures.

rules.name: The Face-Per-Weight Rule
rules.body: Both families ship as 4-style groups, so Medium / SemiBold / ExtraBold are separate families that fontFamily + fontWeight cannot reach. Overriding a weight must switch the face. Typography.tsx resolves this centrally; a screen that sets fontWeight by hand gets the base face and the "all weights look identical" bug.

rules.name: The Growing Box Rule
rules.body: React Native scales fontSize and lineHeight with the system text size; a container measured in dp does not scale with them. Every box that holds text uses minHeight, never height. Asserted by __tests__/theme/fontScale.test.ts.

rules.name: The Dense Rule
rules.body: The design sets ~1.4 leading on prose and leaves the font's tight metric leading on single-line list rows. Pass dense for a row; without it every row renders ~9dp taller than the design.

rules.name: The Tonal-First Rule
rules.body: Reach for a tonal level, then a hairline, then — only if the object truly floats — a shadow. depth.sm and depth.md exist and are currently unused; that is correct, not an oversight.

rules.name: The Type Floor (unsettled)
rules.body: 13 is the floor of the role scale, but 76 call sites across 18 files override fontSize down to 12, 11 or 10 — including every metadatum with legal weight on the inbox. This is recorded as an open decision rather than a rule, because nothing enforces it and an earlier draft of DESIGN.md asserted it held when it did not.

dos: Do take every colour from useTheme(). scripts/check-no-raw-hex.sh fails the build on a raw hex literal outside the sanctioned palette files.
Do use minHeight on anything containing text, so it grows with the system text size.
Do derive a touch target from the drawn size with touchSlop(). A control may be drawn smaller than 48dp — the switch is 48×28, a segment is 34 — but its touch area never is.
Do reserve space for anything that will arrive later. A spinner, a chip or a badge that appears must not move the content around it (constitution V).
Do reach for a tonal level first, a hairline second, and a shadow only if the thing floats.
Do put a new shared pattern in src/theme/ and then use it everywhere it applies. Three components in this repo were written to prevent drift and then adopted once each; the drift happened anyway.
donts: Don't use Alert.alert or any other system dialog. The app draws its own; enforced by __tests__/theme/noSystemAlert.test.ts with no allowlist.
Don't paint an on-<x> token on anything but <x>. Use on-solid for white-on-a-fixed-fill.
Don't spend gold on a second thing. One accent, one job.
Don't hand-tune spacing, radii or type per screen. The same pattern keeps the same numbers; a value that differs from the scale is a bug, not a refinement.
Don't animate anything that was not asked for. Motion answers an action; it never decorates one. Every animation yields to Reduce Motion, and the haptic and focus change survive when it does.
Don't write a docstring asserting a measured property without a test that measures it. Three comments in this codebase promised contrast ratios that had silently stopped being true.
